transcript.text: Can you describe your role and key learnings during your eight-week summer internship at the national research institute?

I'm a final-year BSc Physics student. Last summer I spent eight weeks as an intern at a national research institute, helping with a thin-film measurement experiment. My job was to record readings, about 120 in all, and plot them. I enjoyed the work but realised that I like asking why a lab's equipment is bought and how projects are chosen more than the experiments. That is why I want an MBA.

You mentioned you enjoyed asking why lab equipment is bought and how projects are chosen. Can you explain how this insight shaped your decision to pursue an MBA and the kind of business problems you are interested in solving?

transcript.text: As secretary of the Physics Association I ran six weekly problem-solving sessions for juniors. Attendance was low at first, so I moved them to the evening after classes and it improved.
